title: probabilistic-failover-gentle-rewind-and-telemetry-sanitizer
author: Amelia Park
description: Motivation: During a regional contention incident we observed rapid failover thrashing and a correlated spike in alert noise caused by high-cardinality telemetry emitted during circuit transitions. This PR introduces a probabilistic failover coordinator that smooths regional handoffs by staggering candidate promotion with a gentle-rewind backoff and reduces alert amplification by sanitizing transitional telemetry dimensions. The goal is to keep SLOs stable under partial regional overload while avoiding noisy alerts and expensive cold-starts. Changeset overview: 1) runtime/failover: add probabilistic failover coordinator that assigns a short randomized stagger window before promoting standby regions. The algorithm is deterministic per-tenant seed to avoid global randomness while breaking synchronized flips across regions. 2) runtime/rewind: implement gentle-rewind timers for KV cache warmup; a short ramp replicates active prefix caching heuristics instead of full rehydration on first request. 3) telemetry/sanitizer: new telemetry sanitizer middleware that collapses transient circuit state labels (circuit_id -> circuit_family) and rate-limits high-cardinality tags during handoff windows to avoid alert storms. 4) routing: soft-backoff policy added to the router so requests are probabilistically diverted to warm standbys rather than immediate hard failover under load spikes. 5) tests and canary: unit + integration tests for coordinator, end-to-end fuzz harness for regional failover sequence, and a canary rollout plan with a 10% traffic cohort and automatic rollback on metric regression. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked (ENG-4027) - [x] unit tests for coordinator and rewind logic - [x] integration tests for staged failover sequences - [x] telemetry migration plan and dashboard updates - [x] canary rollout manifest and rollback hook - [x] updated release notes What changed (commits): - \"init probabilistic coordinator and deterministic seeding\" - \"gentle rewind: incremental cache warmup and backoff timers\" - \"telemetry sanitizer middleware and tag collapsing rules\" - \"router: soft-backoff diversion policy and canary flags\" - \"tests: unit, integration, and failover fuzz harness\" - \"observability: dashboards and alerts tuned to sanitized dimensions\" Files touched (high level): - runtime/failover/coordinator.go: new coordinator + docs - runtime/cache/rewind.go: new gentle rewind implementation - router/soft_backoff.go: routing diversion logic and weighting - telemetry/sanitizer/middleware.go: tag collapsing, rate-limiter - telemetry/dashboards/failover_overview.json: dashboard changes - tests/failover/fuzz_harness.go: reproduce fast-flip scenarios - deploy/canaries/failover-canary.yaml: canary rollout config - docs/operations/failover-playbook.md: operator playbook updates - scripts/rollback-hooks/metrics_gate.sh: automated rollback gate Why this approach: Prior solutions used deterministic immediate failover which led to synchronized thrash when multiple regions re-evaluated health at the same time. Staggered probabilistic promotion preserves availability by allowing a small window for overloaded nodes to recover while avoiding large fanouts of cold-starts. Gentle rewind reduces the cost of bringing KV caches into steady-state and reduces latency spikes during handoffs. Telemetry sanitization is critical to prevent alerting systems from being overloaded with transient, high-cardinality signals during normal rebalancing. Testing and rollout: Unit tests validate coordinator decisions with mocked clocks and seeded randomness. Integration tests create multi-region scenarios (simulated latency and exhaust) and assert that SLO regressions are within the allowed tolerance. Fuzz harness enumerates flip sequences to catch edge cases. Canary: 10% traffic in eu-west-1 for 24 hours with automatic rollback if p50 or error-rate drift beyond configured thresholds. Rollout uses staged increments and health checks. Observability and alerts: New dashboard summarizes stagger windows, active promotions, cache warmup progress, and sanitized telemetry counts. Existing SLO enforcer alert rules were adjusted to reference the new sanitized tag \"circuit_family\" instead of raw circuit ids during the canary period. Backwards compatibility and migration: Telemetry sanitizer introduces a temporary compatibility mode where both raw and sanitized tags are emitted for 48 hours in canary to allow downstream alerting teams to switch. After 48 hours the raw tag emission is disabled. Operator playbook includes steps to revert tag emission immediately if necessary. Performance: Microbenchmarks show the coordinator adds an average 0.3ms to routing decision latency with a 95th percentile of 1.1ms under load, but reduces cross-region rehydration token cost by ~28% in our synthetic traffic tests. Hotfix rationale: This was submitted as a hotfix branch because the incident impact on customer SLOs and PagerDuty noise warranted a fast-track fix and careful canary. Security notes: No new external surface; seed generation uses tenant-scoped HMAC with existing platform secret. No credentials in code. Deployment notes: Uses feature flag platform.failover_probabilistic and runtime flag gentle_rewind_enabled; default off for main, enabled in canary manifest. Rollback plan: Flip feature flags off (immediate effect) and run metrics gate script to verify rollbacks. Related: SUP-1882 (support case about noisy failovers), ENG-4027 design doc. Please see CI and review threads below for iteration history.

review_comments: Diego Ramos: Nice approach. Two asks: 1) can we make the seeded randomness reproducible across restarts? 2) add more unit tests around boundary backoff times. See inline for small nits.
Amelia Park: Thanks Diego — coordinator seed is derived from tenant HMAC + last-promote-timestamp; added deterministic seed persistence and documented it. Added boundary tests for 0/1 windows.
Priya Nair: Telemetry sanitizer looks good but we need to ensure downstream dashboards are not broken. Please add a migration note in the dashboards json and notify SRE channels.
Amelia Park: Added migration note and temporary dual-emission mode for 48h. Notified #sre-observability.
Liam Chen: Canary gating looks reasonable. Please confirm rollback hook will actually drain the canary cohort before turning off flags.
Amelia Park: Rollback hook will set canary traffic to 0 and then toggle flags; added additional wait-for-drain check in metrics_gate.sh.

QA (Ruth Miller): Ran integration scenarios, observed reduced flip rate and smaller alert counts in the canary. Found one edge case where a tenant with many tiny KV prefixes saw slower warmup — mitigated by increasing ramp step ceiling; updated rewind.go accordingly.
release_notes: Add probabilistic failover coordinator to reduce synchronized regional failovers; enabled behind feature flag.
Introduce 'gentle rewind' cache warmup to reduce cold-start latency during handoffs.
Add telemetry sanitizer to collapse transient circuit dimensions to 'circuit_family' and rate-limit high-cardinality tags during handoff windows.
Canary rollout: 10% traffic in eu-west-1; dual-emission telemetry for 48 hours during canary.
notes_for_ops: Feature flags: platform.failover_probabilistic=false by default; gentle_rewind_enabled=false by default.
Canary manifest: deploy/canaries/failover-canary.yaml. Start canary with tools/deploy canary --manifest ...
Rollback: run scripts/rollback-hooks/metrics_gate.sh then flip flags off.
Dashboards: telemetry/dashboards/failover_overview.json - new sanitized views. Notify #sre-observability before enabling global.
